AgentMessage.description: A message from the agent to the runner.

oneOf.description: The handshake succeeded.
The handshake failed; the runner exits.
A parse job.

files.description: The files to import, relative to the root, in order.

sys_path.description: Directories put first on `sys.path` (every DAG root).

oneOf.description: A task attempt.

dag_id.description: The DAG's ID (the file may define several DAGs).

inputs.description: The upstream outputs the task uses, by task ID, as stored JSON.

outcomes.description:
The upstream tasks' outcomes, by task ID: a name, or `null` for a skipped one (its
references stand for `None`).

sys_path.description: Directories put first on `sys.path` (every DAG root).

task.description: The task as stored in DAG JSON (its arguments and settings).

oneOf.description: The fork server's preload list (its mode's request).

preload.description: The modules to import, in order (none for the bare fork server).

oneOf.description: Start a runner process (to the fork server).

id.description: The request's ID, repeated in the answer.

mode.description:
What the process runs (`parse` or `task`); it shakes hands on its channel as a spawned
runner does.

oneOf.description: A string run by a shell; interpolated values are shell-quoted unless `raw`.
A program and its arguments, run without a shell; each element is one argument.

Dag.description: A DAG: its identity, trigger, tasks and dependencies.

description.description: A description shown in the UI.

groups.description: The task groups (decision 64), for the UI and the API; the master schedules tasks only.

initial_since.description: `since` of the run on the DAG's first fire time (see PROJECT.md, Runs).

max_active_runs.description: At most this many runs at a time; `None` for no limit.

produced_by.description: The schedr version whose runner produced this JSON.

tags.description: Tags shown in the UI and used for filtering.

trigger.description: What starts its runs (besides people and other DAGs).

DagCtxField.description: A field of the run's context, `dag_ctx.run.*` and `dag_ctx.dag_id`.

oneOf.description: `dag_ctx.run.id`.
`dag_ctx.run.kind`.
`dag_ctx.run.planned_for`.
`dag_ctx.run.since`.
`dag_ctx.dag_id`.

path.description: The file's path relative to the root.

root_dir.description: The root's directory on this worker.

DagLocation.description: Where a DAG is defined: a DAG root and a file path relative to it.

path.description: The file's path relative to the root, with `/` separators.

root.description: The root's name (see PROJECT.md, DAG roots).

Edge.description: A dependency: `to` runs after `from`, when `from` ended with one of the outcomes `on`.

on.description:
The upstream outcomes the edge is taken on (`.on(...)`); empty for any outcome. An edge
not taken counts as skipped in the downstream task's trigger rule.

EdgeKind.description: Why one task depends on another.

oneOf.description: The downstream task takes the upstream task's output (or a part of it).
An order-only dependency (`>>`), no data passed.
From a `@branch` task: taken when the branch chose the downstream task.

ErrorSummary.description: A structured error summary: why a DAG file couldn't be imported, or why a task failed.

exception.description:
The exception's class name, e.g. `ModuleNotFoundError`; `ParseTimeout` or
`RunnerDied` when the agent stopped a file that took too long or lost its runner.

traceback.description: The last lines of the traceback (empty for a timeout).

Expand.description: What a mapped task's instances vary over (decision 69): one instance per element.

oneOf.description:
`.expand(name=values, ...)`: each argument a list (a literal or a reference to a list),
in the order written; the instances are their cartesian product, the first argument
varying slowest (decision 79).
`.expand_kwargs(values)`: a list of dicts, each one instance's arguments.

Field.description: A named field of a `TypedDict` or dataclass.

required.description: Whether the field must be present (`TypedDict`) or has no default (dataclass).

Group.description:
A group of tasks (`with group("load"):`): a name for some of a DAG's tasks, drawn as a box
around them in the UI. It has no state and no rule of its own (decision 56A).

id.description: The group's ID, unique within its DAG (`load`, `load.eu` for a nested one).

parent.description: The group it is nested in, if any.

Mapped.description: One mapped argument of `.expand(...)`: its name and the list it maps over.

value.description: Its list: a literal, or a reference to a list.

OutcomeDecl.description: One of a task's outcomes: its name, and for a `command` task the exit code meaning it.

exit_code.description: A `command` task's exit code for it; none for other tasks.

name.description: The name (an `Outcome` enum member's, a class's, or `None`).

anyOf.description: A dataclass field or dictionary key.

PathElem.description: One step of a path into an output: a field or key, or a list / tuple index.

ProcessUsage.description: What a process used, with the children it reaped: its parent's view at its exit (`rusage`).

involuntary_context_switches.description: Times it was preempted; `None` as for `voluntary_context_switches`.

peak_rss_bytes.description:
The peak resident set size, in bytes. For a forked process it includes the pages it
shares with the fork server (the watchdog's PSS doesn't); `None` for a spawned process
(its memory is gone before the agent reads its zombie).

system_cpu_micros.description: CPU time in the kernel, in microseconds.

user_cpu_micros.description: CPU time in user mode, in microseconds.

voluntary_context_switches.description:
Times it gave up the CPU (waiting for I/O or a lock), with its threads and reaped
children; `None` for a spawned process (its zombie's `/proc` has the leader thread's
only).

Reference.description: A reference to data known only at run time.

oneOf.description: An upstream task's output, or a part of it.

on.description:
The outcomes it was narrowed to (`.on(...)`); empty for any. On another outcome,
or a skipped upstream task, it stands for `null`.

path.description: The path into the output; empty for the whole output.

oneOf.description: An upstream task's outcome itself (`.outcome`), as its name.
A field of the run's context.

RunIf.description:
A task's trigger rule: what its upstream edges must have done for it to run (see
PROJECT.md, Outcomes, failures and joins). An edge not taken counts as skipped.

oneOf.description:
Every edge that wasn't skipped succeeded, and at least one did: skipped when all were
skipped, `upstream_failed` when one failed.

Every edge succeeded: `upstream_failed` when one failed, otherwise skipped when one
was skipped.

RunInfo.description: The run information a task gets (`dag_ctx` and the `SCHEDR_*` variables).

map_index.description: The instance of a mapped task.

planned_for.description: The moment the run is for.

since.description: The start of the run's window.

RunKind.description: Who or what created a run.

oneOf.description: Created by the scheduler for a fire time.
Started by a person (UI, CLI, API).
One of the runs of a backfill.
Created by another DAG's run (`TriggerDagOperator`).
Created by an event from the DAG's trigger (an event trigger).

RunnerMessage.description: A message from the runner to the agent.

oneOf.description: The first message: who is speaking and what for.

mode.description: The mode the runner was started in.

schedr_version.description: The installed `schedr` package version; it must equal the agent's.

oneOf.description: The runner starts importing a file (the agent times each file).

path.description: The file's path relative to the root.

oneOf.description: A file was imported, or failed to import.

dags.description: The DAGs it defines (none for a helper module).

error.description: Why importing it failed, if it did; then `dags` is empty.

path.description: The file's path relative to the root.

warnings.description:
The Python warnings importing it raised (`Category: message`), e.g. a
`TypingHint`.

oneOf.description: Every requested file was handled.

The task's DAG file is imported and its arguments built; its function is called next
(the agent times the start from it). Not sent when that fails.
The task's function returned; its output is encoded and within the size limit.

outcome.description: The outcome's name: `SUCCESS`, an outcome union member's class name, or an `Outcome` member's name.

output.description: The output as stored JSON (tagged extra types).

oneOf.description: The task failed: an exception, or an output that can't be stored.

kind.description:
A failure schedr recognises, e.g. `output_not_serializable`; `None` for an
exception from the task's own code.

oneOf.description:
The fork server preloaded its libraries and is single-threaded: it takes `fork`
requests.

The fork server can't be used: tasks fall back (to the bare fork server, then to
spawn). It answers every later `fork` with `fork_failed` until the agent closes the
channel (exiting with a request unread would reset the connection and could lose this
message). Also the answer to a `fork` when a thread appeared since the check.

reason.description: Why, e.g. a failing preload or a second thread.

threads.description: The names of the threads besides the main one (`/proc/self/task/*/comm`).

oneOf.description: A `fork` request was carried out: the shim runs, and reports on the status socket.
A `fork` request failed; the task falls back.

From the shim, on the status socket: the forked process runs in its own process group
(its ID is the PID), so the agent may signal and watch the group.

pid.description: The process's PID, which is also its process group's ID.

oneOf.description:
From the shim, on the status socket: the forked process ended. The shim reaps it when
the agent closes its end, so the PID isn't reused before.

code.description: The exit code, if it exited.

core_dumped.description: Whether it dumped core (ended by a signal).

signal.description: The signal that ended it, if one did.

usage.description: What it used, with the children it reaped; `None` if the shim couldn't read it.

RunnerMode.description: What the runner was started to do.

oneOf.description: Import DAG files and report the DAGs they define.
Run one task attempt.
Preload libraries, then fork a process per request (Linux only).
A `@task` function, found by task ID when the runner imports the DAG file.

branch.description:
A `@branch` task: its output is the list of the downstream task IDs it chose, and
its outgoing edges are selection edges.

oneOf.description: An inline command, run by the agent.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the process.

oneOf.description: An `EmptyOperator`: completed by the master, no process.

expand.description:
What its instances vary over, for a mapped task (`.expand(...)`); its `arguments` are
then the fixed ones (`.partial(...)`).

group.description: The group it belongs to (the innermost), if any (decision 64).

id.description: The task's ID, unique within its DAG.

outcomes.description: The outcomes it may end with (see PROJECT.md, Task results and outcomes).

output_type.description: The type of its output (`process_result` for commands, `none` for empty tasks).

TaskSettings.description: A task's settings, resolved from its own arguments and the defaults that apply to it.

fresh_process.description:
A Python task: always a new process, never forked (for code that misbehaves after a
fork). Not for other tasks.

max_output_size.description: The output size limit in bytes.

preload.description:
A Python task: fork it from the preloaded fork server (`false`: only from the bare
one, for code that misbehaves next to the preloaded libraries). Not for other tasks.

queue.description: The queue the task goes to.

retries.description: How many times a failed attempt is retried.

retry_delay_ms.description: The delay before each retry, in milliseconds.

run_if.description: When it runs, from its upstream edges (its trigger rule).

timeout_ms.description: The attempt's timeout in milliseconds; `None` for no timeout.

Template.description: A t-string as data: its parts in order.

TemplatePart.description: One part of a template: literal text, or a reference filled in at run time.

oneOf.description: Literal text.
A reference, rendered at run time.

TemplateRef.description: A reference inside a template, with its optional format spec (e.g. `raw`, `%Y-%m-%d`).

oneOf.description: An upstream task's output, or a part of it.

on.description:
The outcomes it was narrowed to (`.on(...)`); empty for any. On another outcome,
or a skipped upstream task, it stands for `null`.

path.description: The path into the output; empty for the whole output.

oneOf.description: An upstream task's outcome itself (`.outcome`), as its name.
A field of the run's context.

format.description: The t-string format spec, if any.

Trigger.description: What starts runs of a DAG besides people (and other DAGs).

oneOf.description: Nothing: manual runs only.
A cron expression (5 or 6 fields, or a preset such as `@daily`) evaluated in a time zone.

catchup.description:
Whether missed fire times get runs in order (`true`) or only the most recent
(`false`).

end.description: The last run it creates is for the last fire time at or before it.

start.description:
The first run it creates is for the first fire time at or after it; without it,
the moment the master first stored the DAG.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone name, e.g. `Europe/Warsaw`; `UTC` by default in the Python API.

oneOf.description: A fixed interval measured in real time (UTC), unaffected by daylight saving.

catchup.description:
Whether missed fire times get runs in order (`true`) or only the most recent
(`false`).

end.description: The last run it creates is for the last fire time at or before it.

interval_ms.description:
The interval in milliseconds; fire times are whole intervals from `start`, or from
the Unix epoch without one.

start.description:
The first run it creates is for the first fire time at or after it; without it,
the moment the master first stored the DAG.

oneOf.description: A single fire time (it has no previous fire time).

TypeDesc.description: The type of a value that can be stored as a task output.

oneOf.description: Anything (an explicit `Any`): only the run-time check applies.
`None`.
`bool`.
`int`.
`float`.
`str`.
`datetime` (stored tagged).
`date` (stored tagged).
`timedelta` (stored tagged).
`list[T]`.
`tuple[A, B, ...]` (stored tagged).
`dict[str, T]` (keys are always strings).
`Literal[...]`.

values.description: The allowed values (strings, integers, booleans or `null`).

oneOf.description: A union, including `Optional[T]` (`T | None`).
A `TypedDict`.
A dataclass.

name.description: The class name, for messages and outcome names.

oneOf.description:
A Pydantic model (decision 59), described by Pydantic's JSON Schema of it: what
`model_dump(mode="json")` writes. Only the Python layer compares it; here its parts
are `Any`.

name.description: The class name, for messages and outcome names.

oneOf.description: The output of a `command` or `script` task.

Value.description:
A task argument: a literal, a reference, a template, or a container of values (so
references inside lists and dictionaries stay visible).

oneOf.description:
A JSON value as encoded by the Python API (with tagged extra types such as
`{"$datetime": "..."}`), passed as is.
A reference, passed with its type (a `date` stays a `date`).
A t-string, rendered to a string.
A list whose elements may contain references.
A dictionary (string keys) whose values may contain references.
